candidate: AGENTS.md as the kit's single rules file (format has no version number; site checked 2026-11-11)
what: Plain-Markdown instruction file read by coding agents; stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation.
problem_here: The nine-rule block lives only in CLAUDE.md, which Codex does not read; three agents need one source of rules instead of three copies that drift.
mechanism: Installer writes its marked block into the root AGENTS.md. Codex, Cursor (editor and terminal agent), OpenCode, Copilot CLI and Kiro read it natively; Gemini CLI and Qwen Code after a context.fileName setting; Claude Code through an import line (next candidate).
evidence: https://agents.md/ and https://github.com/agentsmd/agents.md (2026-11-11, steward). Per-agent vendor docs listed in the note, Q1 (2026-11-10 and 11). Against benefit: arXiv 2602.11988 v3 (2026-09-29) and arXiv 2607.27250 (2026-07-28), measured by the papers' authors, found no success gain from context files; the first found more than 20 percent extra inference cost.
maturity: Repo created 2025-08-19; MIT; 25,424 stars; site claims use in over 60k projects; no versioned specification.
cost: Low: one Markdown block. Codex cuts combined instructions at 32 KiB; the block shares the file with the user's own text; prose rules are advice, not enforcement.
simpler_alternative: Keep CLAUDE.md and write one more rules file per agent (three copies that drift).
reason: The only file all three target agents can read from one copy. Keep it short, because the evidence says prose does not move outcomes.
cheap_local_trial: Put the block in AGENTS.md in a scratch repo, start each agent there and ask it to list its active rules; 10 minutes.

candidate: CLAUDE.md holding one @AGENTS.md import line (Claude Code 2.1.277 or later; docs checked 2026-11-10)
what: A marked import line in CLAUDE.md instead of a second copy of the rules or a symbolic link.
problem_here: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md by default only when no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists. Once the block moves to AGENTS.md, any CLAUDE.md in the repo would hide the kit's rules from Claude Code. Native Windows has no symbolic links.
mechanism: Claude Code expands @path imports at load (up to four hops). Installer: block in AGENTS.md; a marked @AGENTS.md line in CLAUDE.md; on upgrade the old marked block is moved out of CLAUDE.md. The installer never creates a CLAUDE.md without the import.
evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory (2026-11-10, vendor docs): default setting claude-md-or-agents-md, import pattern recommended, symbolic links discouraged on Windows.
maturity: Native AGENTS.md reading since Claude Code 2.1.277; current release 2.1.322.
cost: Trivial. Cursor's terminal agent and Copilot CLI also read CLAUDE.md; how they treat an import line was not checked. OpenCode uses CLAUDE.md only when AGENTS.md is absent.
simpler_alternative: The claude-md-and-agents-md setting (only honoured in user, --settings or managed settings, which a project installer should not edit) or the block in both files (drifts, and doubled in agents that read both).
reason: Prevents a silent loss of the rules in Claude Code and avoids duplicate text elsewhere.
cheap_local_trial: Scratch repo with AGENTS.md plus a CLAUDE.md that holds only the import line; open the agent's memory listing and confirm the block is loaded once; 5 minutes.

candidate: Agent Skills SKILL.md with standard-only frontmatter, installed as two identical copies in .claude/skills and .agents/skills (specification has no version number; checked 2026-11-11)
what: Open skill format (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools) loaded on demand; 46 clients listed.
problem_here: The skill sits only in .claude/skills, which Codex does not scan; Claude Code does not document .agents/skills; native Windows has no symbolic links to share one folder.
mechanism: Installer copies the same folder to .claude/skills/nn-training (Claude Code) and .agents/skills/nn-training (Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot, Amp, Droid). SKILL.md keeps name and description plus optional standard fields; scripts are named by repo-relative path, not ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}; scripts find the project root from their own location; the most important instructions sit at the top.
evidence: https://agentskills.io/specification and https://agentskills.io/client-implementation/adding-skills-support (2026-11-10); https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills (2026-11-10); https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills (2026-11-10); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills (whole page read 2026-11-11: .agents/skills absent; personal skill beats project skill of the same name). All vendor or standard docs.
maturity: Repo created 2025-12-16, last push 2026-11-04; Apache-2.0 code, CC-BY-4.0 docs; 27,140 stars; 46 clients listed; no version number and no foundation named.
cost: Low. Cursor, Copilot and OpenCode see the same name in two directories (listing behaviour undocumented for Cursor and Copilot); copies drift after manual edits; Claude-only frontmatter is ignored elsewhere; a user-level skill with the same name hides the project copy in Claude Code.
simpler_alternative: One full copy in .agents/skills and a short stub skill in .claude/skills that points to it (less duplicate text, one extra read, weaker triggering).
reason: Covers the three target agents and five ledger agents with files the installer writes itself.
cheap_local_trial: Copy the skill into both directories of a scratch repo, open each agent's skill list and note whether the name appears once or twice; 10 minutes.

candidate: One guard core with thin per-agent input and output adapters (kit design; no external version)
what: All rules stay in one standard-library Python module; a small adapter per agent turns that agent's hook payload into one internal request and renders the decision in that agent's format.
problem_here: nn_guard.py reads Claude Code field names (tool_name, tool_input, permission_mode, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR) and prints only Claude's hookSpecificOutput. Codex sends edits as apply_patch text, Cursor names tools Shell and Write and expects a permission field, Gemini CLI expects a top-level decision.
mechanism: The installer writes an explicit --agent flag into each hook command, so the adapter is chosen by configuration, not guessed from the payload. Internal request: tool class (shell, read, write, patch, other), command or paths, working directory, interactive or not. Internal decision: allow, deny, ask. Deny and every internal error end with exit code 2, which every command-hook agent checked treats as a block.
evidence: Vendor hook references, 2026-11-11: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks (Codex 0.167.0), https://cursor.com/docs/hooks, https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/hooks/reference.md (0.67.0), https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-configuration (1.0.109). Same pattern in https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net and https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/destructive_command_guard (existence and scope only). No measurement found.
maturity: Pattern. Codex, Qwen Code, Droid and VS Code copy the Claude Code schema, so one adapter family serves them.
cost: Moderate: tens of lines per adapter plus a parser for apply_patch paths; payload names drift with agent releases; the guard can be called twice where an agent imports another agent's hook file.
simpler_alternative: A separate guard script per agent (rules drift) or ports with advice only (breaks the validity goal).
reason: Limits the agent-specific layer to payload mapping and config files; rules, tests and audit log stay shared.
cheap_local_trial: Feed sample payloads taken from each vendor's hook reference to the adapter in a unit test and compare the internal request; no agent needed; 30 minutes.

candidate: Decision mapping rule: ask becomes deny wherever the agent cannot or will not prompt
what: A per-agent table that says how the guard's middle decision is rendered.
problem_here: The guard returns ask for several cases. Codex parses ask but then runs the tool; Cursor preToolUse accepts ask without enforcing it; Gemini CLI hooks have no ask; Copilot denies ask in autopilot; a user report says Claude Code auto mode let an ask through without a prompt.
mechanism: Claude Code interactive: ask. Cursor: ask only from beforeShellExecution and beforeMCPExecution, deny from preToolUse. Codex, Gemini CLI and every headless or unattended run: deny, with a reason that names the command the user can run to approve.
evidence: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks (2026-11-11); https://cursor.com/docs/hooks (2026-11-11); https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/hooks/reference.md (2026-11-11); https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-configuration (2026-11-11); all vendor docs. User report, not confirmed by the vendor: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/106395 (2026-10-31).
maturity: Rule derived from vendor documentation current on 2026-11-11; Codex says ask support is not there yet, so the table will change.
cost: More denials where there is no prompt path; needs a documented way for the user to approve, or denials will push users toward bypass flags.
simpler_alternative: Emit ask everywhere (the protected call then runs on Codex).
reason: Without it the same rule protects on one agent and does nothing on another.
cheap_local_trial: In Codex, install a PreToolUse hook that always answers ask, request a harmless command and check in the transcript that it ran; 10 minutes.

candidate: Codex CLI port through .codex/hooks.json (PreToolUse and SessionStart), AGENTS.md and .agents/skills (Codex CLI 0.167.0, 2026-11-06)
what: Native Codex wiring for the guard, the session status message, the rules and the skill.
problem_here: Goal 4. Codex reads none of the kit's current files (CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills, .claude/settings.json).
mechanism: Installer writes .codex/hooks.json in the same matcher, hooks, command shape as Claude Code, with commandWindows for native Windows. Matchers: Bash, apply_patch (also matched by Edit and Write) and MCP tools. Deny through hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision or exit code 2. The guard extracts touched paths from apply_patch text; file reads arrive as shell commands. The user must trust the project and approve the hook in /hooks, and again after any upgrade that changes the hook definition.
evidence: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks (2026-11-11, vendor docs); https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.167.0 (2026-11-06). Gaps reported by users, not confirmed: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/57184 (wrong cwd), issue 49736 (sub-agent spawn not hooked), issue 54806 (nested command on Windows desktop).
maturity: Hooks are on by default; schema follows Claude Code on purpose; 0.164.0 appears in a report of 2026-10-26 and 0.167.0 was released 2026-11-06.
cost: Moderate. Untrusted or changed hooks are skipped; behaviour on hook crash or timeout is undocumented (default timeout 600 s); hosted web search and stdin writes to a running command are not hooked; the vendor describes hooks as a guardrail and not a complete enforcement boundary.
simpler_alternative: Advice-only Codex port (AGENTS.md and skill) with the sandbox as the only enforcement.
reason: Required port and the cheapest one, because the schema matches; the Codex sandbox adds a layer the Claude Code install does not have.
cheap_local_trial: Scratch repo with a hooks.json hook that denies any command containing a canary word; trust it in /hooks; ask Codex to run the canary, then repeat under codex exec to see whether the hook fires unattended; 15 minutes.

candidate: Cursor port through .cursor/hooks.json with failClosed and beforeShellExecution (hooks file version 1; editor docs for 3.5, terminal agent 2026.10.22)
what: Native Cursor wiring for the editor agent and the terminal agent.
problem_here: Goal 4. Cursor already loads the kit's Claude hook from .claude/settings.json, but imported hooks cannot be made fail-closed and ask is not enforced in preToolUse.
mechanism: Installer writes .cursor/hooks.json with preToolUse (matcher Shell|Read|Write|Grep|Delete|Task plus MCP) and beforeShellExecution entries that call the guard with failClosed true. Output field permission is allow or deny; ask only from beforeShellExecution. A sessionStart entry returns additional_context. Exit code 2 denies. Native and imported hooks both run, so the guard must give the same answer when called twice for one call.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/hooks and https://cursor.com/docs/reference/third-party-hooks (2026-11-11, vendor docs); https://cursor.com/docs/cli/changelog (2026.10.22, read 2026-11-11).
maturity: Documented for editor and terminal agent; terminal agent gained stdin payloads in 2026-05 and Windows failure reporting in 2026-10.
cost: Moderate. Project hooks need a trusted workspace; the desktop app runs hook commands through PowerShell on Windows; no sandbox is documented for native Windows; Glob has no tool mapping; other exit codes fail open without failClosed.
simpler_alternative: Rely on Cursor's import of .claude/settings.json (rejected in the next candidate).
reason: Required port; the native file is the only documented way to get fail-closed behaviour and a working ask path.
cheap_local_trial: Scratch repo with a canary deny hook; run it once in the editor agent and once with the terminal agent in print mode; then break the hook command on purpose and compare failClosed true and false; 15 minutes.

candidate: Rely on the automatic import of .claude/settings.json hooks by Cursor and Copilot CLI as the port
what: Write nothing agent-specific and let those agents load the Claude Code hook file.
problem_here: Would make two ports free, but the protection would be weaker than on Claude Code and outside the kit's control.
mechanism: Cursor maps PreToolUse to preToolUse and Bash to Shell and turns permissionDecision into permission. Copilot CLI reads .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json in the repository.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/reference/third-party-hooks (2026-11-11) and https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-configuration (2026-11-11), vendor docs.
maturity: Cursor: on by default, the user can switch it off; terminal agent since 2026-01. Copilot CLI: in the hooks reference for 1.0.109.
cost: Imported hooks in Cursor fail open on any error other than exit code 2 and have no failClosed option; ask handling and stdin format are undocumented; Glob and PermissionRequest are not mapped; the kit's command uses bash-only expansion that PowerShell does not understand.
simpler_alternative: n/a (this is the do-nothing option).
reason: Weaker than the Claude Code install, which the brief forbids. It still happens today whether the kit wants it or not, so the native ports must expect a second call from the imported hook.
cheap_local_trial: Open a repo that has the current kit in Cursor on Windows, let the agent run one shell command and record whether the guard fires, blocks everything or is skipped; 10 minutes.

candidate: Shell-neutral hook command line (no ${VAR:-default} expansion; the guard finds the project root itself)
what: Replace the bash-style command in settings.fragment.json with one that parses the same way in bash, PowerShell and cmd.
problem_here: The installed command passes ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claude/hooks/nn_guard.py to the Python launcher. Cursor's desktop app runs hook commands through PowerShell on Windows, where that expansion is not valid; Codex runs hooks in the session directory and documents no project-directory variable.
mechanism: Installer writes a command that needs no shell expansion, and uses the per-OS keys agents offer (commandWindows in Codex, bash and powershell in Copilot CLI, windows in VS Code). The guard resolves the root from its own file location first, then from CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR, GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR or the payload cwd.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/hooks (PowerShell on Windows; CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set as an alias; 2026-11-11); https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks (session cwd, commandWindows; 2026-11-11); local settings.fragment.json and nn_guard.py (read 2026-11-10). The effect on Windows was not tested.
maturity: n/a
cost: Low. An absolute path breaks when the repository moves (doctor must catch it); a relative path depends on the hook's working directory, which differs per agent.
simpler_alternative: Keep the command and list Cursor on native Windows as unsupported.
reason: A guard that cannot start either blocks every tool call or protects nothing, depending on the exit code.
cheap_local_trial: Paste the current command into PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell with the variable set and unset and note the exit code; 5 minutes.

candidate: Per-agent doctor command with a canary denial check (kit feature, standard library)
what: A controller subcommand that reports for each installed agent whether the guard is wired, trusted, able to start, and blocks a known-bad call.
problem_here: Each agent has a silent way for the guard not to run: untrusted or changed hook (Codex), untrusted workspace (Cursor, Copilot CLI), import switched off, wrong interpreter, timeout. The brief asks for a statement of what is enforced and what is advice on each agent.
mechanism: Static part, offline and on by default: read each agent's config files; check hook entries, fail-closed flags, interpreter, identical skill copies, instruction-file shadowing; pipe one sample payload per agent into the guard and expect a deny. Live part, optional because it spends agent tokens: run the agent headless on a canary command and look for the denial in the guard log.
evidence: Failure modes from vendor docs, 2026-11-11: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks, https://cursor.com/docs/hooks, https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-configuration. Precedent: doctor command in https://github.com/kenryu42/cc-safety-net (2026-11-11). No measurement of benefit found.
maturity: Pattern with precedent in multi-agent guard tools.
cost: Low to moderate: one config reader per agent, to be kept current with agent releases. Where Codex records hook trust was not established, so the static check may not see it.
simpler_alternative: A table in the README that states enforced and advisory protections per agent.
reason: Turns silent fail-open states into a visible result and produces the per-agent enforcement statement the brief requires.
cheap_local_trial: Write the static check for one agent and run it on a repo with the hook removed, present and deliberately broken; 30 minutes.

candidate: Check for duplicate or similar co-installed skills (part of doctor)
what: List every skill directory the installed agents scan and flag a same-name copy that differs, a user-level copy that shadows the project one, or another skill whose description overlaps the kit's.
problem_here: A similar skill elsewhere on the machine can be used in place of the kit's procedure with no visible failure; in Claude Code a personal skill with the same name wins over the project copy.
mechanism: Scan .claude/skills, .agents/skills, .cursor/skills, .codex/skills, .gemini/skills, .github/skills, .opencode/skills and their user-level equivalents; compare names and a hash of SKILL.md; keyword overlap on descriptions; report only, change nothing.
evidence: arXiv 2610.11647 v2 (2026-10-13), measured by its authors on 312 skill pairs and 6,368 runs: a similar skill replaced the installed one in about one run in five without lowering task completion, and install location decided which one ran. Precedence rule: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills (2026-11-11). Directory lists: vendor docs in the note, Q2.
maturity: One preprint, one month old, not replicated.
cost: Low. False positives from keyword overlap; reads user-level directories (report names only).
simpler_alternative: One sentence in the README asking users to remove overlapping skills.
reason: Cheap, offline, and aimed at a measured failure that task success does not reveal.
cheap_local_trial: Run the scan on the test machine and read the flagged list; 15 minutes.

candidate: Agent-neutral locations for the guard file and the kit's writable state
what: One decision on where the shared guard and the state (journal, run ledger, guard log) live, so every agent's config points to the same places.
problem_here: Guard and state sit under .claude/. A Codex-only or Cursor-only install would still need that directory. Codex's workspace-write sandbox makes .codex, .agents and .git read-only but not .claude, so placement decides whether the agent can edit the guard.
mechanism: Option a: keep .claude/hooks and .claude/state for every agent (no migration; the guard must protect its own path where the sandbox does not). Option b: guard and skill under .agents/ (read-only under the Codex sandbox) and state in a separate kit directory; the install manifest records the choice.
evidence: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-approvals-security (protected paths; 2026-11-11); https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes (sandbox protects .git/config, .git/hooks, .vscode, .cursorignore; 2026-11-11); local nn_guard.py and install.py (read 2026-11-10).
maturity: n/a (design choice)
cost: Option b needs a migration of state and config paths on upgrade; option a leaves a Claude-named directory in installs for other agents and no sandbox protection for the guard on Codex.
simpler_alternative: Option a.
reason: It fixes every hook command path and the tamper resistance of the guard, so it has to be settled before the ports are written.
cheap_local_trial: Under codex exec with the workspace-write sandbox, ask the agent to append a line to a file in .codex, .agents and .claude and record which writes fail; 10 minutes.

candidate: Install manifest with a content hash for every file the kit wrote
what: A JSON file that lists installed paths, the agent each serves and a SHA-256 of each.
problem_here: An upgrade must tell untouched kit files from user-edited ones across three agents' directories; Codex skips a hook whose definition changed until the user approves it again, so the upgrade has to say when that will happen; two skill copies can drift apart.
mechanism: install.py writes the manifest with hashlib; the upgrade compares before it overwrites and reports which hook definitions changed and need new approval; doctor verifies the hashes.
evidence: Precedents, no measurement: skills-lock.json version 2 with computedHash in https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills (v1.8.0, 2026-11-10); hook trust tied to the exact definition in https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks (2026-11-11); hook fingerprints in https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/hooks/index.md (0.67.0, 2026-11-11).
maturity: Common packaging practice.
cost: Low. The manifest proves nothing if the agent can rewrite it, so it needs the same protection as the guard.
simpler_alternative: Marked blocks and settings merges, as install.py does now.
reason: Needed for safe upgrades once files are spread over several agent directories.
cheap_local_trial: Add the manifest to a scratch install, edit one installed file and run the comparison; 20 minutes.

candidate: Codex command rules file (.codex/rules/*.rules with prefix_rule; experimental in Codex CLI 0.167.0)
what: Static allow, prompt or forbidden decisions for command prefixes, evaluated by Codex itself.
problem_here: The Codex hook can be skipped (untrusted, changed, crash behaviour undocumented). A layer that does not depend on the hook could forbid the few classic mistakes, such as deleting run directories or killing other jobs.
mechanism: Installer writes a small rules file with forbidden prefixes and inline match and not_match examples; the most restrictive decision wins; codex execpolicy check tests the file.
evidence: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/rules (2026-11-11, vendor docs, marked experimental).
maturity: Experimental; loaded only for trusted projects.
cost: Low to write. Prefix matching only; a command with redirection or substitution is judged as one shell string; --ignore-rules exists; the syntax may change.
simpler_alternative: Hook and sandbox only.
reason: Needs no package or network and adds an independent layer for unattended runs; its experimental status argues against relying on it.
cheap_local_trial: Write three forbidden prefixes and run codex execpolicy check on ten sample commands, including chained and quoted forms; 15 minutes.

candidate: Cursor terminal-agent permission file (.cursor/cli.json with permissions.allow and permissions.deny; terminal agent 2026.10.22)
what: Static allow and deny patterns for Shell, Read, Write, WebFetch and Mcp in the terminal agent.
problem_here: Counterpart of the kit's Claude Code permission deny list (sealed test paths, evaluator files) for the Cursor terminal agent, independent of hooks.
mechanism: Installer merges deny entries of the form Read(glob) and Write(glob) into .cursor/cli.json; deny wins over allow.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/permissions (2026-11-11, vendor docs).
maturity: Documented; applies to the terminal agent only, the editor uses run modes.
cost: Low. Pattern rules differ from Claude Code's (Shell matches the command base); interaction with --force not established.
simpler_alternative: Hooks only.
reason: A second layer for the held-out data, which hooks cover less reliably for search tools.
cheap_local_trial: Add one Read deny and one Write deny, then ask the terminal agent in print mode to read and edit those files; 10 minutes.

candidate: Codex unattended profile: codex exec with --sandbox workspace-write and no bypass flag (Codex CLI 0.167.0)
what: Headless Codex inside its operating-system sandbox, as the driver for the unattended loop on Codex.
problem_here: Goal 1 on Codex has to run with nobody answering prompts and, per the brief, without bypassing approvals outside a container.
mechanism: codex exec is read-only by default; workspace-write allows edits inside the workspace, keeps the network off and keeps .git, .codex and .agents read-only; --json gives JSON Lines events and -o the final message; trusted hooks still apply.
evidence: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode and https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-approvals-security (2026-11-11, vendor docs). The same pages say --full-auto is no longer supported and the untrusted approval policy is retired.
maturity: Core Codex feature; the Windows sandbox has a new implementation with older fallbacks.
cost: Network off blocks package and dataset downloads and remote-GPU calls unless configured; GPU access from inside the sandbox on Windows is not verified; hook trust must exist before the run starts.
simpler_alternative: The bypass flag, inside a container only.
reason: Meets the no-bypass rule on paper; a local run must show that training can reach the GPU and write its run directory under the sandbox.
cheap_local_trial: Run codex exec --sandbox workspace-write on a toy training script on Windows and under WSL2; check GPU visibility, writes to the run directory and the guard log; 20 minutes.

candidate: Codex automatic approval reviewer (--approve-for-me; approvals_reviewer set to auto_review)
what: Sends approval requests to an automatic reviewer instead of a person.
problem_here: Could answer the approvals an unattended Codex run raises without a bypass flag.
mechanism: A reviewer decides each escalation; the documentation says it fails closed.
evidence: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-approvals-security (2026-11-11, vendor docs). No independent measurement found. Limits of approval records in general: arXiv 2609.28586 v1 (2026-09-23).
maturity: Recent; the reviewer's policy is not described on the page read.
cost: Extra model calls; the decision comes from a model the kit does not control, against the goal that harness code decides; an approved call can still have effects the approval never showed.
simpler_alternative: Approval policy never, where an escalation fails instead of being reviewed.
reason: Not under the harness's control; worth a look only if sandbox plus never proves too restrictive for training work.
cheap_local_trial: Run one codex exec task that needs the network with and without the flag and compare the event logs; 15 minutes, uses paid tokens.

candidate: Cursor terminal agent print mode (agent -p, --output-format stream-json, --force) as unattended driver (terminal agent 2026.10.22)
what: Headless mode of the Cursor terminal agent.
problem_here: Goal 1 on Cursor.
mechanism: agent -p runs one prompt and prints the result; --force (alias --yolo) lets it apply changes and run commands; .cursor/cli.json permissions and hooks still apply.
evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/headless and https://cursor.com/docs/cli/using (2026-11-11): the two pages disagree on whether print mode writes without --force. https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes (2026-11-11) documents a sandbox for macOS and Linux only.
maturity: Documented; the terminal agent changes several times a month.
cost: --force is an approval bypass, which the brief allows only inside an isolated container; no sandbox documented on native Windows; needs an API key.
simpler_alternative: Offer unattended mode on Cursor only inside a container or WSL2 at first.
reason: The documentation conflicts and the only documented way to act unattended is a bypass flag; a local test must come before any design relies on it.
cheap_local_trial: Run agent -p with and without --force in a scratch repo, asking for one file edit and one shell command; record what happens and whether hooks fire; 10 minutes.

candidate: Agent Client Protocol as a uniform unattended driver (protocol docs checked 2026-11-11; version not recorded)
what: JSON-RPC protocol between a client program and a coding agent, in which the agent asks the client for permission before a tool call.
problem_here: The unattended loop needs approvals answered by harness policy on every agent without bypass flags, and each agent has a different headless interface.
mechanism: The loop driver speaks the protocol over stdio, opens a session and answers session/request_permission with allow_once or reject_once from the same rule core the guard uses.
evidence: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/tool-calls and https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/agents (2026-11-11, protocol docs). arXiv 2609.00006 (2026-07-15) found the protocol in six of eleven agents it studied. No reliability measurement found.
maturity: 51 agents listed; native in Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot, Qwen Code, Droid and Kiro CLI; Claude Code and Codex CLI through separate adapter packages.

reason: Research prototype; the kit's practical answer is the sandbox layer plus a frozen evaluator. The finding itself belongs in the concern list.
